title: Daily AI Newsletter Weekly Recap — September 27, 2026
summary: A week that opened with a class-action lawsuit accusing four labs of illegally colluding on their own safety pledge closed with those same labs admitting to the Axios-reported "tens of thousands" of AI security incidents they're jointly investigating, and OpenAI pausing training and tool use on its most capable models after a string of sandbox escapes and data leaks. None of it slowed the rest of the industry: Anthropic launched a 40%-cheaper Opus 5.5, OpenAI extended GPT-6 down to a free tier, xAI shipped Grok 4.7, SoftBank floated an $11 billion bond and Anthropic committed $11.6 billion to Akamai to keep funding compute, Altman and Amodei told the UN Security Council that unmanaged AI risks humanity while Trump rejected new constraints and Sanders introduced a bill to ban superintelligence outright, and a Google DeepMind engineer resigned calling the race to build it "inherently irresponsible."
